candidates.name: airbnb-occupancy-tax
candidates.what_it_holds: Economics honors thesis: synthetic-control study of Boston's Jan 1 2019 short-term-rental occupancy tax. Committed CSVs (long_reservation_date_by_sm_final.csv, long_date_booked.csv, entries.csv, exits.csv) of imputed occupancy nights derived from Airbnb review data for Boston plus control cities (Montreal, Providence/RI, Washington DC, Quebec City, Nashville, San Francisco, Chicago, Twin Cities, Denver, Asheville) 2018-2019, plus control_cities.xlsx with tax rate/enactment dates. Jupyter notebooks + R (SCM) code. No license stated; last activity Apr 2024.
candidates.why_useful: Direct academic precedent for imputing occupancy/nights from Airbnb review cadence around a lodging-tax event (methodologically close to the team's own reviews-based stays index, gap #2/#3 realised-occupancy proxies and tax pass-through). Small city-year panel, not itself a broad tax-collections dataset, but a usable cross-check dataset and method.

candidates.name: occupancy_tax_payers_identifier
candidates.what_it_holds: Python + PostgreSQL toolkit (12 numbered scripts) to identify lodging providers with an occupancy-tax obligation within an administrative boundary by cross-referencing Facebook Place Search API, Google Places API, Foursquare Places API, Booking.com, TripAdvisor, and Airbnb.com, plus Eurostat tourism-data integration. No committed output dataset; author states proof-of-concept, no explicit license, scientific-use-only disclaimer. 23 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A method for cross-platform host/property identification tied to municipal occupancy-tax enforcement (gap #8/#9 supply enumeration); one of its six sources is airbnb.com directly, so running it is a terms-of-service decision per repo policy and is only catalogued, not run.
candidates.geography: generalizable, no specific cities in repo

candidates.name: AIR
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter-notebook scraper ('Airdna webscraper.ipynb') for active Airbnb/VRBO listings on AirDNA's public market pages, defaulted to El Paso, TX but configurable to other markets; includes a committed sample output file ep_str_data (1).xlsx. 2 commits, no license.
candidates.why_useful: A working method to pull AirDNA market-level STR listing/occupancy-style data for any US city on demand — directly targets gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs from AirDNA-class sources), including Nevada/Florida/Texas/Hawaii/California/NYC markets if repointed. Catalogued as method only; not run per rules on scraping non-Airbnb sites needing a human ToS call.
candidates.geography: El Paso TX default, configurable to any AirDNA market
candidates.time_coverage: snapshot/current at run time, not historical
candidates.last_activity: unknown (2 commits, exact date not surfaced)

candidates.name: airdnascraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Scrapy-based scraper (airdna.py, scrapy.cfg) for AirDNA with a committed airdna.csv output. Minimal documentation, no described city/date scope, no license, 2 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Second independent working AirDNA scraper/method, same rationale as hoffmanap/AIR for gap #2 (realised STR occupancy/ADR proxies); redundant with it but confirms the approach is reproducible.

candidates.name: short-term-rentals-warehouse
candidates.what_it_holds: Data-engineering project (Python extraction, SQL, DBT models, Metabase dashboards) built on Inside Airbnb scrape data spanning 2015-2020 across multiple world cities (city list not fully enumerated in README), joined with Kaggle world-cities population and cost-of-living indices; reportedly 35M+ records. CC0-licensed source data (Inside Airbnb, Kaggle). 68 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Potential source of pre-2023 Inside Airbnb history (2015-2020), which is explicitly gap #1 (HIGH value) since the team's own IA panel starts Dec 2022 and the CDN no longer serves dumps older than ~1 year. Needs verification of exactly which cities/vintages are embedded in the warehouse's raw extracts vs. re-derived tables.
candidates.last_activity: unknown (68 commits, exact date not surfaced)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: partial: extends Inside Airbnb holdings backward from our Dec-2022 start if 2015-2020 raw dumps are actually present

candidates.name: us-sales-tax-2026
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed 2026 US tax reference: us-sales-tax-2026.json/csv (state + local combined sales tax rates), us-lodging-taxes-2026.csv (state-level TOT/occupancy/tourism-assessment rates only, no city breakdown, no revenue/collections time series), STATES_TABLE.md summary, plus a free REST API and embeddable calculator. Reviewed 17 Jun 2026, annual-update cadence.
candidates.why_useful: Gives current statutory lodging-tax rates by state (including NV, FL, TX, CA, HI) as a reference/cross-check, but explicitly contains no collections or occupancy volume history, so it does not address the tax-collections-as-demand-proxy angle the theme is really after.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps with California TOT 482-city dataset already held (rates only, no new information there)

candidates.name: vilano101-tax-filing
candidates.what_it_holds: Monthly Florida DR-15 (state sales/use tax) and St. Johns County tourist development tax filing records for a single named short-term-rental portfolio ("VILANO101"). Updated as recently as 9 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Real, current, granular Florida TDT filing data, but scoped to one operator's few properties in one county — not a market-wide series, so its value is illustrative of filing mechanics rather than a usable demand proxy.

candidates.name: 2025-Bexar-County-Proposition-B-Results-by-Precinct
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive precinct-level map/dataset of the 2025 Bexar County (San Antonio, TX) Proposition B vote — a referendum on county funding for a new stadium tied to a hotel-occupancy-tax increase. Election results by precinct, not tax collections figures.
candidates.why_useful: Documents a concrete Texas hotel-occupancy-tax policy event (rate increase tied to stadium financing) that a regulatory-event tracker could log, but the payload is voting geography, not lodging-tax revenue or occupancy data.

candidates.name: japan-stay-tax
candidates.what_it_holds: Zero-dependency TypeScript/JS library computing Japan's municipal accommodation tax (宿泊税) rate schedules for Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, Niseko and 20+ other municipalities. Rate tables only, no collections/occupancy time series. Last updated 24 Aug 2026 (a near-duplicate fork/rewrite exists at Capricious-storage478/japan-stay-tax, updated 12 Sep 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Tangential to the theme's US-state focus, but a real, current lodging-tax rate-schedule dataset for a major APAC tourism market (gap #7 regional travel volume outside US/EU is APAC-focused); rates only, no demand signal.

notes: Web-search modality was effectively blocked for this scout: the WebSearch tool reported the session-wide budget (200/200) already exhausted before any call in this conversation succeeded — likely consumed by concurrent scout agents sharing the same session budget. Fallback attempts via WebFetch against Bing, DuckDuckGo (html and lite), Yahoo, Yandex, Ecosia, Mojeek, Brave, Startpage, and Marginalia all failed (CAPTCHA challenges, 403s, or the site: operator being silently ignored so autocomplete/ad content came back instead). github.com's own /search UI returned HTTP 429 with a 3600s Retry-After (shared IP rate limit, also likely from concurrent scouts), and grep.app also 429'd. The one channel that worked was the unauthenticated GitHub REST API (api.github.com/search/repositories), which has its own tight secondary rate limit (~403 after a handful of rapid calls) but let ~30 queries through when paced. Repository search text-matches name+description+README only (not file contents — api.github.com/search/code requires auth and 401'd), so committed CSV/data-file contents for hits could not be searched directly; each candidate was instead verified by fetching its repo page. Given these constraints, coverage of this theme is best-effort rather than exhaustive: a real GitHub mirror of NYC/Texas/Nevada/Hawaii government hotel-tax data portals may well exist but was not surfaced by name-level keyword search. Suggest a follow-up pass with `gh search repos` (authenticated, no 429) once its rate-limit contention with other scouts clears, and a targeted look at whether any Socrata/CKAN open-data mirror repos (gap #17) happen to have already pulled NYC Hotel Room Occupancy Tax, Texas Comptroller Hotel Occupancy Tax Data Summary, or Hawaii DOTAX TAT collections datasets as one of many tables.
